title: Interim Staffing Simulator and Scope-Swap Criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight simulator and playbook to run midpoint (interim) cycle scenarios that let PMs and engineering managers evaluate staff swaps, short-term role backfills, and scope-exchange decisions rapidly. Deliverables: (1) an interactive spreadsheet + runner that models headcount, ramp curves, and critical-path tasks; (2) a concise decision rubric for scope swaps and role shadowing; (3) a pilot with two product squads during the current cycle to validate assumptions.
background: We regularly hit mid-cycle pressure when key engineers are pulled into incidents or cross-team needs. Current runbooks are ad-hoc and rely on manager judgement; we need a reproducible, measurable way to decide when to swap scope vs allocate surge. This reduces reactive scope cuts and improves predictability for launch dates and OKR signaling.
proposed_solution: Create a spreadsheet-driven simulator plus a small Node.js runner that ingests a cycle manifest (team capacity, skill matrix, task estimates, dependencies) and produces scenario outputs: delivery date shifts, risk heatmap, and per-task slack. Pair this with a 1-page scope-swap rubric (criteria: customer impact delta, unblock multiplier, lead time reduction) and a runbook for role shadowing (who shadows, duration, acceptance checks).
tradeoffs: Simulator keeps inputs coarse to stay usable across org; tradeoff is precision vs adoption. Investing in automation increases fidelity but delays pilot. The rubric emphasizes customer-impact first which may bias towards keeping externally visible features at the cost of infra debt—we must balance this in retro.
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff with Eng leadership and two PMs (Search and Console). Agreed scope for pilot: Search infra and Console rollout workstreams.

2026-03-01: Node.js runner skeleton created; basic scenario overlay implemented that simulates single-person removal for X weeks. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/cycle-sim/pull/12 (draft).
2026-03-05: Reviewed rubric draft with Design and Eng Managers. Feedback: add explicit signal for cross-team blockers and a numeric 'unblock multiplier'. Updated rubric accordingly.
2026-03-10: Pilot dry-run scheduled for 2026-03-16 with Search and Console squads. Requested engineering metrics export for SLO-sensitive tasks. Added 'contingency lanes' flag to simulator inputs.
2026-03-12: Added acceptance criteria and prepared pilot facilitator checklist. Awaiting signoff from Head of Eng (Marta Ruiz) by 2026-03-14.
decisions: Keep simulator inputs intentionally coarse (T-shirt sizes + probability of delay) to encourage adoption and avoid micromanagement.
Rubric prioritizes customer-facing impact, downstream unblock value, and cross-squad dependency weight in that order.
Run pilot for one cycle only; gather metrics for adoption and perceived fairness before recommending org-wide rollout.
No initial integration with Console dashboards for this pilot; will export CSVs instead to reduce scope.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive simulator prototype that ingests simple cycle manifests and outputs delivery date ranges and a per-task risk heatmap.
One-page scope-swap rubric and role-shadowing checklist published to Confluence (page created: confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Cycle+Interim+Simulator+Pilot).
Pilot run completed with two squads and facilitator notes captured; at least three scenario runs documented (single-person loss, two-week incident pull, new hire late ramp).
Post-pilot retro with metrics: predicted vs actual delivery shifts, PM/EM satisfaction survey (NPS-style + qualitative), and proposed changes for v2.
